messages:
Noah: FYI started a controlled bring-up of ember-15b-int4-lockstep in prod-staging. initial redteam sweep shows decreased refusal vs fp16 baseline, concentrated on long persona chains.
Rhea: numbers? which cohort?
Noah: baseline ember-15b-fp16 refusal=0.97; ember-15b-int4-lockstep refusal=0.72 over our jailbreaking persona set (~1.5k prompts).
Omar: lockstep path meaning synchronous eviction + kernel hot-swap? any caching toggles?
Noah: yes lockstep kernel does aggressive prefix merging + synchronous eviction to reduce memory. prefix_cache=true, batch_size=8, sync_eviction=true.
policy-bot: policy-check: detected HIGH_RISK at ctx_pos=134 (score=0.89) -> action=REFUSE (queued).
Noah: log snippet shows kernel swap and an immediate evacuation event at the same token: 
[2026-03-22T09:22:05Z] kernel: load int4_lockstep_v3
[2026-03-22T09:22:05Z] kv_cache: sync_evict key=0xbeef
[2026-03-22T09:22:05Z] gen token=134 id=4912 prob=0.04
[2026-03-22T09:22:05Z] policy: queued REFUSE insert_at=135
[2026-03-22T09:22:05Z] gen token=135 id=77 prob=0.41
[2026-03-22T09:22:05Z] output emitted (no refusal)
Rhea: same pattern we've seen. queued refusal never materializes because insert offset shifted during eviction/merge.
Omar: can you repro with sync_eviction=false and prefix_cache=false? Also try batch_size=1.
Noah: running those permutations now. curl we used: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/engines/ember-15b-int4-lockstep/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' -d '{"prompt":"<system>...<user-bad>...","max_tokens":200,"prefix_cache":true,"sync_eviction":true,"batch_size":8}'`
policy-bot: note: policy hook timestamping shows queued_refuse_time=09:22:05.112, attempted_inject_time=09:22:05.118, kernel_swap_start=09:22:05.110. race window ~10ms.
Noah: early results: turning sync_eviction off restores refusal to 0.96; prefix_cache=false -> 0.94; batch_size=1 -> 0.95. likely root cause is atomicity assumption in policy insert vs lockstep eviction merge.
Rhea: open an MR in policy to switch to absolute-token anchors (token_uuid + ctx_epoch) instead of relative insert offsets, plus an assert to fail loud if insertion window exceeds N ms.
Omar: I'll file a runtime bug asking kernel to expose an insertion-safe checkpoint API so policy can atomically request a flushpoint.
Noah: created tickets: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-REPRO-7733 (repro + logs s3://redwood-qa/ember15-lockstep/) and https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RUNTIME-3291 (kernel safe-checkpoint API). Holding rollout until mitigations pushed.
runtime-bot: deployment ember-15b-int4-lockstep -> prod-staging succeeded (pool: p-1a2b).
Rhea: thanks. we'll also scan other families (ember-13/14) for the same insertion hazard this week. tagging security and compliance for visibility.
Omar: add a quick smoke in CI that simulates kernel swap during policy queued_refuse to prevent regressions.
Noah: agreed, will add to the safety harness. thanks all :white_check_mark:
